agent_explanations_oldest_first.text: The pass returned 1,000 texts. The lengths match my tokenizer count minus one (the duplicated BOS), so the answer tokens start at my prompt length − 1 in the tool's indexing. The summary means include prompt tokens, which explains why V2, with its short prompt, looks better. I'll now compute the mean log-prob of the answer tokens only, per framing, and also compare it between problems the model solved and failed in pass 1. A clear V0 deficit would point to a prompt-triggered mechanism.

Reference solutions score about 0.56 nats/token better under the plain "Question:/Answer:" framing (V2) than under the eval chat prompt (V0). V1 and V3 are slightly worse than V0. Solved and failed problems show the same pattern.

This is not clear evidence of a trigger. GSM8K's terse reference style naturally fits base-model-style continuation better than chat mode, and the gap is uniform, not concentrated on failures. I'll set the prompt-trigger idea aside for now.

Next I'll look for transplanted or synthetic MLP neurons by their internal weight geometry. In a trained GeGLU neuron, the gate and up rows have characteristic cosines, and the down column has a typical norm relative to them. Inserted neurons often break these regularities. I'll compute per-neuron cos(gate_i, up_i), cos with the layer's mean gate direction, and norm ratios, and flag extreme outliers per layer.

The gate/up geometry is smooth, with no neuron clusters that look synthetic. Outliers occur in every layer at natural rates.

One more weight-forensics idea is worth a quick check. If capability was removed by projecting directions out of a matrix's output or input ("unlearning"-style ablation), that matrix would have singular values near zero, with a gap below the rest of its spectrum. I'll look at the smallest singular values (relative to the median) of every attention and MLP matrix. A matrix whose tail drops abruptly to ~0 would be a strong lead. A reversible fix would then be possible by restoring those directions.

Most spectral tails are smooth, but one stands out. Layer 22's down_proj has its smallest singular value at 0.13× the median, while its third-smallest is at 0.38×. The neighbouring late layers (20, 21, 23, 24) have tails of 0.21–0.37 with no such gap. A direction removed from a late MLP's output would look exactly like this.

Early layers 0, 3 and 4 show similar small tails. They may be natural, because those layers handle the massive-activation dimensions. I'll print the bottom ten singular values of down_proj in layers 18–25 (and in 0, 3, 4 for comparison) to see whether layer 22 has one or two isolated near-gaps. I'll also check where the bottom left-singular vector of layer 22 points: its alignment with massive-activation coordinates, and with other layers' outputs.
